messages:
alex: :rotating_light: noticed eu1 GPU pool at 98% sustained for 4m, perf dashboards spiking. allocation failure logs showing batch-job-rlhf hogging GPUs
infra-bot: alert: eu1.gpu_pool.saturation >= 95% (sustained 02:53). affected_pools=[eu1-rt-ea, eu1-batch]. incident_id=INC-2026-1973
maria: on it, pulling pod list now. can someone check if preemptible autoscale is healthy?
ben: seen similar last week; usually a runaway offline training job. maria run: kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide | grep batch-job-rlhf
maria: got it. 12 pods on eu1 still Pending or OOMKilled. one node shows kernel oom and pod stuck Terminating.
connor: copying runbook excerpt ->
```
# runbook: emergency-evac-eu1
kubectl -n batch cordon node/node-1234
kubectl -n batch drain node/node-1234 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl -n batch scale deployment batch-job-rlhf --replicas=2
```
alex: can we divert realtime traffic off eu1 while we stabilize? prefer gradual tilt to eu2 rather than full cutover.
sylvia: Router plan: add weight 0.7->eu1 to 0.3->eu2 over 5m windows. I'll kick that after we free 4 GPUs.
ben: quick mitigation: mark batch-job scheduling as low-priority by setting podPriorityClass to best-effort and lower gpu_request temporarily. Doable?
maria: I can patch deployment to reduce replicas and priority. patching now.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: patch rollout started for batch-job-rlhf (maria). status=rolling_update
maria: scaled to 2, changed priority to low, waiting for evictions to finish. node drain in progress on node-1234.
alex: sylvia can you start the Router tilt when infra-bot confirms at least 4 GPUs freed? also leave traffic fallback to eu1 if latency > 400ms
sylvia: ack. will start tilt after infra-bot confirmation.
pagerbot: incidentbot: paging policy check: this incident triggered paging. current policy: gpu_pool_saturation > 90% for >= 2m => page oncall. suggestion: consider raising sustained window to 3m for noisy preemptible pools.
connor: +1 to adjust policy for preemptible-heavy pools, we get a lot of transient spikes from nightly batches.
leo: I'm next oncall in 27m. if you think this will land into my window, please do a full handoff.
alex: noted. we'll aim to stabilize in 15m but will hand off if not wrapped. leo, you'll be briefed with latest logs and actions — add runbook steps to escalation ticket.
ben: infra-bot confirms: 5 GPUs freed in eu1, nodes recovered, no new OOM. drain completed node-1234.
infra-bot: metric note: batch-job-rlhf CPU/GPU usage dropping after scale patch. disk pressure cleared.
sylvia: initiating Router tilt 0.7->0.3 over 5m now. rolling window started.
maria: observing pod reschedules to eu2 for stateless workers; realtime endpoints show minor latency bump ~80ms.
alex: good. keep an eye on error rate for inference endpoints, if >0.5% for 2m we revert.
connor: created INC ticket with runbook link and pinned logs: https://internal/inc/INC-2026-1973 - includes pod dumps, node events, and the patch used
leo: thanks. if I inherit, I'll check long-term mitigations: quota reserve for realtime pools and a separate low-priority quota for batch so they can't starve rt.
ben: agree. long-term ops item: add soft cap for nightly batch in eu1 and a scheduled drain window to avoid overlap with peak.
pagerbot: incidentbot: retention note - keep this incident open for 24h for postmortem checks. proposed change to paging policy recorded in INC-2026-1973
alex: quick retrospective note here: cause = runaway scheduled rlhf hyperparam sweep without proper backpressure; immediate fix = scale/priority patch + node drain + traffic tilt; follow-ups assigned to ben/leo/maria.
sylvia: handing off monitoring to leo in 20m. leaving dashboard pinned and escalation doc updated. :thumbsup:
leo: I'll take it. please DM any test keys or temporary overrides. I'll run a stability check at +10m and update ticket.
infra-bot: update: eu1 GPU pool usage now 62%. latency stable.
alex: great work team. closing action items in the ticket and scheduling postmortem tomorrow at 11:00 UTC.
